verses.1: After this, Jesus went across the sea of Galilee, to Tiberias.
verses.2: And a large crowd followed him, because they saw the signs he made for the sick people.
verses.3: Then Jesus went into the mountain, and there he sat down with his disciples.
verses.4: It was a time of fasting, the day of fasting for the Jews.
verses.5: Then Jesus opened his eyes and, seeing a large crowd approaching him, he said to Philip, “Where can we buy enough bread for all these people to eat?”
verses.6: And this was what he said, trying to figure out what he should do. After all, he knew exactly what he was supposed to do.
verses.7: Philip replied to him: “Six hundred days isn’t enough time for them to get any food, so that each of them can have a little bit.”
verses.8: One of his disciples said to him, Andreas, the brother of Simon Peter.
verses.9: It’s a child, after all, who has five slices of bread and two apples. But what’s the point of all that for someone like him?
verses.10: Jesus said, “Make the people rise up.” There was a large crowd in that place. In total, there were about fifty thousand men who were able to get up.
verses.11: So, Jesus took the bread and blessed it, then he gave it to those who were there. He also gave them as much of the wine as they wanted.
verses.12: And as they were affected by this, he said to his disciples, “Collect the extra seeds, so that no one will be killed.”
verses.13: So, they took twelve kopius each from the five kinds of bread that were given to the beggars.
verses.14: So, those people who saw what he did, said that he truly was the prophet who would come into the world.
verses.15: Jesus, knowing that he would be captured and taken away so that they could make him a king, once again refused to go into the mountain alone.
verses.16: And when his vision came about, his disciples went down to the sea.
verses.17: And as they boarded the ship and sailed across the sea towards Kafarnaum, darkness already covered the sky. Then Jesus appeared to them.
verses.18: And the sea was filled with the wind of a great storm.
verses.19: So they watched Jesus walking on the sea for about twenty-five or thirty stadia. They were terrified.
verses.20: And he said to them, “I am, do not be afraid.”
verses.21: So, he wanted to take him on the ship. And immediately, the ship arrived at the shore where they were going.
verses.22: In the evening, when the crowd stood on the shore by the sea, they saw that there was no ship there at all. They also realized that Jesus did not go with his disciples onto the ship; instead, only his disciples went away.
verses.23: But ships came from Tiberiad, near the place where we ate the bread, in thanksgiving to the Lord.
verses.24: When the crowd saw that Jesus wasn’t there, along with his disciples, they rushed onto the boats and went to Capharnaum, seeking out Jesus.
verses.25: And when they found him beyond the sea, they said to him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?”
verses.26: Jesus replied to them, “Yes, I tell you. You are not asking for signs to see; rather, you are asking for the ability to eat from the food and to be filled.”
verses.27: Work not to find the lost one, but rather the one who remains alive for eternal life. For this is the gift that the Son of Man will give you. This has been promised by God.
verses.28: So I said to him, “What shall we do so that we can carry out the works of God?”
verses.29: Jesus replied to them, “This is the work of God: that you believe in Him whom He has sent.”
verses.30: I said to him, “What sign then will you show us, so that we may believe in you? What action will you take?”
verses.31: Our fathers ate the fruit of the tree in the wilderness, as it is written. He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
verses.32: So Jesus said to them, “I truly tell you, it is not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven. It is my Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.”
verses.33: For the bread of God is that which ascends from heaven and gives life to the world.
verses.34: I said to him, “Lord, please always provide us with this bread.”
verses.35: Jesus said to them, “I am the Bread of Life. Whoever comes to me will not go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be lost.”
verses.36: But I said to you that even your friends don’t believe me.
verses.37: Everything that my father gives me, I will keep for myself. And I won’t let anyone who comes to see me go out with it.
verses.38: Because I was sent from heaven not to fulfill my own desires, but those of the one who sent me.
verses.39: This is then the desire of the one who sent me: that I not lose anything of what has been given to me, but instead, I should rise again on the last day.
verses.40: This is therefore the desire of my father: that everyone who considers the son and believes in him to have eternal life, may be raised by me on that last day.
verses.41: So, the Jews said about him, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
verses.42: And they said, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph? We know his father and mother. How can he now say that he descended from heaven?”
verses.43: Jesus replied to them, “Do not be concerned with one another.”
verses.44: No one can come to me unless my father sends me to arrest him. I will surely bring him before me on that last day.
verses.45: It is written in the prophets: And all those who are teachers of God’s word will be teachers as well. Anyone who hears from their parents and learns from them will come to me.
verses.46: Not only did he see the father as being one who belonged to God, but he also saw him as a true father.
verses.47: I say to you truly, those who believe have eternal life.
verses.48: I am the bread of life.
verses.49: Your fathers ate the fruit of the tree in the wilderness and died.
verses.50: This is the bread that comes from heaven, so that people can eat it and not die.
verses.51: I am the bread that comes down from heaven. If anyone eats this bread, he will live forever. And the flesh I give you is for the life of the world.
verses.52: So, the Jews said to each other, “How can he possibly give us his body to eat?”
verses.53: Then Jesus said to them, “Truly, I say to you, if you do not eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in yourselves.”
verses.54: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life. I will raise him from the dead on that last day.
verses.55: For my flesh is indeed a source of strength, and my blood is indeed a source of nourishment.
verses.56: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me.
verses.57: Just as my living father sent me away, so too do I live because of him. And those who feed me will also live because of me.
verses.58: This is the bread that came down from heaven. It wasn’t like the fathers who ate it and died. Those who eat this bread will live forever.
verses.59: These words were spoken during a teaching session in Kafarnauum.
verses.60: Many people, upon hearing what his disciples said, said, “This is a harsh statement. Who can possibly listen to such words?”
verses.61: But Jesus knew in himself that his disciples would be confused about this. He said to them, “Is this something that confuses you?”
verses.62: So, if you consider the son of man as being moving back to where he used to be?
verses.63: Breath is what gives life; the body itself is of no use at all. The words I have spoken to you are both breath and life.
verses.64: But there are some among you who do not believe. For from the beginning, Jesus knew who those who did not believe were, and who they were.
verses.65: And he said, “For this reason, I tell you that no one can come to me unless he is drawn to me by God himself.”
verses.66: As a result, many of his disciples left him and no longer followed him anymore.
verses.67: So Jesus said to the twelve: “Do you also want to go away?”
verses.68: Simon Peter replied to him, “Lord, for what purpose should we leave here? You have the words of eternal life.”
verses.69: And we have come to believe and know that you are indeed the holy one of God.
verses.70: Jesus said to them, “Have I not chosen you out from among all the people? And one of you will be the devil.”
verses.71: He referred to Judas Iscariot. This man was one of the twelve who were about to deliver him up.
